subject: Critical Thinking
title: How Fake News Spreads: The Anatomy of a Viral Lie
description: A 60-second lesson on How Fake News Spreads: The Anatomy of a Viral Lie.

hook.text: MIT study (2018): false news spreads 6x faster than true news on Twitter. Lies travel light. Truth is heavy.

buildup.text: False news succeeds because it's novel, emotional, and simple. True news is often complex, nuanced, and boring.

discovery.text: Vosoughi et al. found that false stories are 70% more likely to be retweeted than true ones.

twist.text: Corrections rarely catch up. By the time a fact-check is published, the false story has reached 10x more people.

climax.text: The sharing impulse is the vulnerability. Slow down, check the source, and resist the urge to be first to share.

punchline.text: A lie gets halfway around the world before the truth puts on its shoes.

quiz.question: Why does false news spread faster than true news?
options: It's more novel, emotional, and simpler than true news

details.summary: False information spreads faster and wider than truth online because it triggers stronger emotional reactions. The anatomy of viral misinformation involves emotional hooks, social validation, algorithmic amplification, and cross-platform spread.
details.whyItMatters: Understanding the mechanics of viral misinformation helps you recognize and resist false stories before you inadvertently amplify them by sharing.
takeaways: False news spreads six times faster than true news on social media
Emotional novelty drives sharing faster than factual accuracy
Each share increases perceived credibility through social proof

faq.question: Why does false information spread faster than accurate information?
faq.answer: MIT research found that false news is more novel and triggers stronger emotional reactions, particularly surprise and disgust. People share content that provokes strong feelings. Truth is often mundane; lies are crafted to be emotionally compelling.

faq.question: What can individuals do to avoid spreading misinformation unknowingly?
faq.answer: Pause before sharing anything that triggers strong emotion. Check the source. Read beyond the headline. Look for the same story in other credible outlets. If you cannot find independent verification, do not share. Speed is the enemy of accuracy.
